text: Organisational behaviour is the study of human behaviour in
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: OB studies how individuals and groups behave within organisations.

text: OB draws knowledge from psychology sociology and
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: OB is interdisciplinary drawing on psychology sociology anthropology and political science.

text: The three levels of analysis in OB are individual group and
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: OB analyses behaviour at the individual group and organisational levels.

text: Organisational behaviour is a purely theoretical field with no practical application
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: OB is applied and helps managers improve productivity satisfaction and effectiveness.

text: State the disciplines that contribute to organisational behaviour
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Psychology sociology social psychology anthropology and political science.
explanation: Each discipline contributes insights at different levels of analysis.

text: Explain the models of organisational behaviour
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: The main models are autocratic custodial supportive and collegial. They differ in the basis of control and in employee orientation moving from obedience to self direction.
explanation: Describe each model and how employee orientation evolves across them.

text: The process by which individuals organise and interpret sensory impressions is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Perception is how people select organise and interpret their sensory environment.

text: Judging someone based on a single characteristic is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: The halo effect lets one trait colour the overall impression of a person.

text: A relatively stable set of characteristics that determines how a person thinks feels and behaves is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Personality is the stable pattern of traits that shapes behaviour.

text: Attitudes have three components cognitive affective and behavioural
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Attitudes consist of belief feeling and intention to act.

text: What are the components of an attitude
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: The cognitive component is the belief the affective component is the feeling and the behavioural component is the intention to act.
explanation: These three components together make up an attitude.

text: Explain the determinants of personality
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Personality is shaped by heredity environment family social and situational factors. Both inherited traits and life experiences combine to form personality.
explanation: Cover the heredity versus environment debate and situational influences.

text: The theory that links effort to performance to reward is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Expectancy theory says motivation depends on expectancy instrumentality and valence.

text: Learning through observing others and imitating their behaviour is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Social learning theory emphasises learning through observation and modelling.

text: Job satisfaction is the positive feeling about a job resulting from evaluating its characteristics
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Job satisfaction is an affective response to the job and its characteristics.

text: Distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Intrinsic motivation comes from the work itself such as interest and achievement. Extrinsic motivation comes from external rewards such as pay and promotion.
explanation: The source of the drive internal or external distinguishes the two.

text: Explain the reinforcement theory of learning
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Reinforcement theory states that behaviour is a function of its consequences. Positive and negative reinforcement strengthen behaviour while punishment and extinction weaken it.
explanation: Describe each type of consequence and its effect on behaviour.

text: The stage of group development marked by conflict over roles is
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: In the storming stage members experience conflict as they establish roles.

text: The tendency of group members to suppress disagreement to maintain harmony is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Groupthink occurs when the desire for consensus overrides realistic appraisal of alternatives.

text: A group is a set of people who interact to achieve individual rather than shared goals
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: A group interacts to achieve shared goals; a team is a group with complementary skills and mutual accountability.

text: List the stages of group development
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Forming storming norming performing and adjourning.
explanation: These are the five stages in Tuckmans model of group development.

text: Explain the difference between a group and a team
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: A group has a common interest and individual accountability while a team has complementary skills shared goals and mutual accountability. Teams achieve synergy that groups may not.
explanation: Cover goals skills accountability and the synergy of teams.

text: The ability to influence others toward the achievement of goals is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Leadership is the process of influencing people to pursue goals willingly.

text: Power that comes from a persons formal position in the hierarchy is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Legitimate power derives from the formal authority of a position.

text: A leader who consults followers before deciding uses a democratic style
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Democratic leaders involve followers in decision making.

text: List the bases of power identified by French and Raven
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Legitimate reward coercive expert and referent power.
explanation: These five bases explain the different sources of a leaders power.

text: Explain the trait and behavioural approaches to leadership
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: The trait approach seeks qualities that distinguish leaders from non leaders. The behavioural approach studies what leaders do such as task orientation and people orientation rather than what they are.
explanation: Contrast the two approaches and give examples of each.

text: The shared beliefs values and norms that guide behaviour in an organisation form its
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Organisational culture is the shared values and assumptions of members.

text: The physical or psychological response to demands that exceed a persons capacity is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Stress is the strain from demands that exceed available coping resources.

text: Positive stress that motivates and improves performance is called eustress
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Eustress is beneficial stress that energises while distress is harmful.

text: Define organisational culture
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Organisational culture is the set of shared values beliefs and norms that members learn and pass on and that distinguish one organisation from another.
explanation: It shapes how members behave and interact.

text: Explain the sources and consequences of stress
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Stress arises from organisational factors like role ambiguity work overload and poor relationships and personal factors. It can cause low performance absenteeism burnout and health problems.
explanation: Cover organisational and personal sources and their consequences.

text: Assertion: Employees with high job satisfaction tend to have lower turnover. Reason: Satisfied employees are more committed and less likely to leave
subject: Organisational Behaviour
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Satisfaction builds commitment which reduces the desire to leave.

text: Match the concept to its meaning
subject: Organisational Behaviour
options: Stereotyping - judging based on group membership|Halo effect - judging each trait independently|Projection - accurate self assessment|Perception - ignoring sensory data
explanation: Stereotyping judges a person by their group while the halo effect generalises one trait.

text: The process of changing an organisation from its current state to a desired future state is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Organisational change moves the organisation toward a planned future state.

text: Lewins three step model of change consists of unfreezing moving and
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Lewins model has unfreezing the change and refreezing stages.

text: Resistance to change is always irrational and never justified
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Resistance may reflect genuine concerns about loss and can be a useful signal.

text: Explain the reasons why employees resist change
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Fear of the unknown habit loss of security and status and mistrust of management cause resistance to change.
explanation: Understanding these reasons helps managers manage change.

text: Read the case: A team misses deadlines because members rarely share information and avoid discussing disagreements to keep peace. Identify the group problem and suggest how to fix it
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: The team is suffering from groupthink which suppresses dissent. The leader should encourage open debate appoint a devils advocate and seek outside opinions before deciding.
explanation: Diagnose groupthink and propose structural remedies to encourage dissent.

text: Read the case: A talented employee has low motivation because she feels her effort does not affect rewards which she does not value. Use expectancy theory to diagnose and suggest a solution
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Expectancy is low because effort does not clearly lead to performance or valued rewards. The manager should clarify the performance reward link and offer rewards the employee actually values.
explanation: Apply expectancy instrumentality and valence to the described symptoms.

text: A managers belief about whether employees are inherently lazy or self motivated is the basis of
subject: Organisational Behaviour
options: Theory X and Theory Y|Trait theory|Path goal theory|Fiedler model
explanation: McGregors Theory X assumes people dislike work while Theory Y assumes they seek responsibility.

text: The Ohio State studies identified two leader behaviours initiating structure and
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Initiating structure is task oriented while consideration is people oriented.

text: The Big Five personality traits include openness conscientiousness extraversion agreeableness and neuroticism
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: These five dimensions are the widely accepted Big Five model of personality.

text: The extent to which a person identifies with a job and considers performance important is called
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Job involvement reflects psychological identification with the job.

text: Explain the relationship between attitudes and behaviour
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Attitudes influence behaviour through intentions but the link is moderated by situational constraints and the strength and specificity of the attitude.
explanation: Specific strong attitudes predict behaviour better than general ones.

text: Explain the importance of organisational behaviour for managers
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: OB helps managers understand predict and influence behaviour. It improves motivation teamwork leadership and the management of change and diversity leading to higher productivity and satisfaction.
explanation: Link OB concepts to practical managerial outcomes.

text: Describe the process of perception and the errors in it
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Perception proceeds through selection organisation and interpretation of stimuli. Errors include stereotyping halo effect projection and selective perception which distort judgement.
explanation: Trace the perceptual process then explain the common perceptual distortions.

text: Job satisfaction is measured only through salary levels
subject: Organisational Behaviour
explanation: Satisfaction depends on many factors including the work itself supervision peers and growth.

text: Explain the types of teams in an organisation
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Teams include problem solving teams self managed teams cross functional teams and virtual teams. They differ in autonomy scope and how members coordinate.
explanation: Describe each team type with its purpose and features.

text: Explain the importance of emotional intelligence in the workplace
subject: Organisational Behaviour
correctAnswer: Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognise and manage ones own emotions and those of others. It improves leadership teamwork conflict resolution and customer relations.
explanation: Cover the components of EI and their workplace benefits.
